title: Introduce token-interleaving fidelity validator and GPU-throttle simulator
author: Maya Chen
release_notes: Adds a token-interleaving fidelity validator and a lightweight GPU throttle simulator used by the benchmark lab to validate correctness/reliability of batching + interleaving under transient GPU contention. No user-facing API changes.
description: Motivation: We have observed intermittent small regressions when model-serving uses aggressive token interleaving combined with dynamic kernel selection under transient GPU contention. These regressions are low-frequency in perf runs and difficult to reproduce with existing drivers. This PR introduces two pieces: 1) a token-interleaving fidelity validator (ti-validator) that replays representative interleaved request streams against a golden model execution trace and flags divergence in token timing/ordering and soft-quality regressions; 2) a GPU-throttle simulator that injects controlled, time-bound reductions in available streaming multiprocessors / simulated clock to exercise scheduling pathologies. The overall goal is to make low-rate correctness/latency anomalies reproducible in CI and local experiments. Changes in this PR: - new bin/ti-validator: a reproducible runner that accepts recorded request traces (jsonl) and a golden token trace, outputs per-step divergence metrics and a small ASCII timeline for quick triage; - new bench/sim/gpu_throttle: small simulator that integrates with the lab harness and toggles simulated capacity windows and per-kernel latency multipliers; - telemetry hooks: per-step tags emitted to the lab metrics pipeline (labels: ti_run_id, throttle_profile, seed); - CI test: a deterministic unit test that runs the ti-validator on a micro-trace and expects zero divergence; - docs: README + usage examples and a short guide for adding new throttle profiles. Checklist: - [x] design doc linked in Linear ENG-9102; - [x] unit + integration tests; - [x] telemetry + tagging; - [x] basic docs and quickstart; - [x] bench harness integration. Commits: ["Initial ti-validator binary and core replay loop (maya/ti-validator)", "Add gpu_throttle simulator and throttle profiles (maya/gpu-sim)", "Telemetry tags + metric adapters (maya/telemetry)", "Tests and docs; fix flakiness in timeline assert (maya/fixes)"] Changed areas (high-level): - bin/ti-validator.py: core replay and divergence heuristics - bench/sim/gpu_throttle.py: capacity windowing and kernel slowdown hooks - lab/harness/injectors.py: small adapter to enable throttle profiles in CI runs - telemetry/adapters/bench_metrics.py: emit tags and counters - tests/ti_validator_test.py: deterministic microtrace test - docs/benchmark-lab/ti-validator.md: usage and adding profiles Review conversation summary: "Arjun: Please add a safety cap on total simulated slowdown; observed a local run stall at 10x slowdown. Response (Maya): Added a global cap and an exponential backoff for the simulator; updated tests to validate no stall. Lina: Can we make the validator tolerant to benign non-determinism (timing jitter) by using a configurable epsilon and sample window? Response (Maya): Added windowed matching with configurable epsilon and documented default thresholds; left a flag --strict for deep debugging. Benji: Telemetry tags look good, but please ensure sensitive payloads are never emitted. Response (Maya): Validator only emits token ids/hashes and timing deltas; added a scrubber and documented privacy bounds. CI notes: Initial run showed one flaky integration test that timed out under simulated throttle; test timeout increased and harness made deterministic by pinning rng seed. Final CI: all checks passed (unit, lint, integration, bench-smoke). Merge: squash-merged into main after approvals from Arjun and Lina. Risk assessment: Low-medium. This is test/harness code only but touches telemetry and the harness adapter; careful when enabling throttle profiles in production-like experiments. How to use: 1) capture trace with bench/recorder; 2) run bin/ti-validator --trace mytrace.jsonl --golden golden.tokens --throttle low_latency_profile; 3) inspect divergence report and timeline.
